title: Whole Pollen and Mineral Tests Branching Rack Scene
description: One newly authored static magnified-morphology teaching arrangement, one scene and zero new independent models. Three whole accepted originals occupy separate finite pads on a new branching three-level rack: whole bisaccate pine pollen at the low front-left station, the complete nested radiolarian skeleton at the middle front-right station, and the whole lobulate foraminifer exterior at the high rear station. A triangular grounded scene-only foot, broad lower branching arms, three rooted risers and three distinct horizontal pads create the support system and clear reading lanes. This is not the previous two-object cell/organelle flat-slab layout with examples exchanged. Every reused object preserves its entire binary mesh payload, normals, indices, all material dictionaries and internal hierarchy at original unit scale; only whole translations are added. No chamber, saccus, pore, beam or spine is extracted, recoloured or counted as a new model. These are different enlarged illustrative scales and unlike biological objects; their displayed sizes do not imply real relative dimensions, a shared organism, mineral chemistry, taxonomic relationship or an actual microscopic sample. Whole foraminifer and radiolarian representations are exterior skeletons; pollen is an opaque exterior grain, not an internal air chamber model. No labels, textures, working instrument, physical load/stability, diagnostic, climate, biological function, rig, animation or interaction claim.
